rule_ids: GO-GATE-01 — Run the ordered gate block (fmt, vet, golangci, go fix -diff, build/test, -race, tidy -diff, govulncheck, generate check) from every go.mod root, gating on exit status
GO-GATE-02 — Run go vet ./... as its own step in every repo; never treat a green go test as a vet pass
GO-GATE-03 — Gate modernization on go fix -diff ./...; do not enable golangci's modernize linter
GO-GATE-04 — Run go test -race ./... on every PR in a job with CGO_ENABLED=1 explicitly set
GO-GATE-05 — When //go:generate exists, gate on go generate ./... && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)", never git diff --exit-code
GO-GATE-06 — Require gofmt-clean output (golangci-lint fmt --diff or gofmt -l empty); goimports SHOULD, gofumpt opt-in
GO-GATE-07 — Run the SDK's and every CLI's tests on windows-latest and macos-latest legs too
GO-GATE-08 — Pin golangci-lint to an exact v2 release in CI; never latest/@latest
GO-GATE-09 — Copy the fleet v2 config verbatim (default: none, explicit list) and require golangci-lint config verify exit 0
GO-GATE-10 — Set issues.uniq-by-line: false and both issue caps to 0
GO-GATE-11 — Enable govet enable-all minus shadow/fieldalignment (nilness replaces disabled SA5011); Go-team repos run standalone nilness
GO-GATE-12 — Configure nolintlint with require-explanation, require-specific, allow-unused: false
GO-GATE-13 — Deny io/ioutil, pkg/errors, golang/mock, x/exp/slices, x/exp/maps, x/xerrors via depguard (plus testify in tests)
GO-GATE-14 — Exclude exactly G104 and G115 in gosec with 0755/0644 perm thresholds, and re-justify excludes on every golangci bump
GO-GATE-15 — Enable revive and gocritic only with explicit rule/check lists (fleet: context-as-argument, deep-exit; exitAfterDefer)
GO-GATE-16 — Never baseline default: all and never enable wsl/exhaustruct/paralleltest/tparallel/nlreturn/varnamelen/goconst/noinlineerr/wrapcheck
GO-GATE-17 — Run exactly one staticcheck entry point; never place staticcheck.conf beside golangci's staticcheck
GO-GATE-18 — Add the CLI overlay (exhaustive, forbidigo on fmt.Print*, gocritic exitAfterDefer) to every CLI module
GO-GATE-19 — Enable bodyclose only in direct net/http packages without body wrappers; keep it out of the baseline (SHOULD)
conflicts_resolved: golangci modernize linter (golangci-config MUST) vs go fix -diff (gate-commands): go fix is the gate — same diagnostics on fixture and zap, but only go fix applies //go:fix inline [C-4]; golangci modernize dropped
Separate go vet step (gate-commands rule 3: skip when golangci govet at defaults) vs always: always run it — cheap, tracks the toolchain, removes a conditional agents misapply
bodyclose as MUST (golangci-config) vs the map's admission clause: 88/88 oras-go hits are wrapper FPs, so it fails; demoted to SHOULD GO-GATE-19
nilness 'not wired into govet' (golangci-config Contested) vs map: govet enable-all runs nilness and is the only check catching a planted nil deref; go vet and staticcheck 2026.2.1 both miss it [C-1]

staticcheck.conf reproduction 'inconclusive' (golangci-config): root cause is staticcheck skipping files under os.UserCacheDir(); with the cache dir moved, standalone honours the conf and golangci's bundled copy ignores it [C-3]
Audit claim that tailscale layers staticcheck.conf under golangci: false — golangci enables no staticcheck (.golangci.yml:9-15) and a standalone job reads the conf; tailscale is the compliant model
omitzero 'changes JSON output' (map M3) vs gate-commands: go fix declines the behaviour-changing alternative by default; gate-commands is right
hostport/waitgroup gated by the go line (gate-commands §2): refuted — both fire under a go 1.21 line on the 1.27.1 toolchain [C-10]
go generate drift via git diff --exit-code (gate-commands rule 7): misses new untracked generated files (exit 0); git status --porcelain required [C-9]
errorlint errorf 'ships off' (map conflict 22) vs 'defaults true' (golangci-config): both right per entry point — true under golangci 2.14.0, standalone go-errorlint needs -errorf (go-errors [C])
revive SHOULD-only (golangci-config) vs GO-CONC needing context-as-argument: revive in baseline with an explicit 2-rule list; a rules list replaces the defaults [C-5]
thelper MUST (GO-TEST-05) vs the <=1 FP/10k bar: admitted with naming/position checks off; 24/95 hits were style, begin hits sampled real [C-6]
wrapcheck SHOULD-with-ignoreSigs (golangci-config) vs not adopted (go-errors): off and in the banned-noise list
Ownership of tidy/-mod=readonly, tool pinning, govulncheck and the generated marker (gate-commands rules 5, 6, 9, 10): assigned to GO-MOD-03/11/12 and GO-CORE-05 and cited, not restated
gosec config: golangci-config excludes list merged with GO-IO's 0755/0644 permission thresholds into one settings block
needs_another_round: bodyclose (GO-NET/GO-GATE) — hand-classify regclient's 78 non-test hits: does bodyclose meet <=1 FP/10k LOC on HTTP-client code that wraps response bodies, or should GO-NET use a reading heuristic?
golangci --fix (M-M-15) — which enabled linters' auto-fixes are behaviour-preserving enough for an unattended agent loop? Only go fix and golangci-lint fmt are cleared today
staticcheck non-default checks (M-M-09) — do ST1000/ST1020-22 meet the FP bar on SDK/library code, and do they duplicate revive 'exported'?
nilnil vs API design (GO-API/GO-ERR) — is (nil, nil) banned across the SDK surface, given the deliberate nil-means-absent hits in ko and oras-go?
exhaustive for the SDK (GO-CLI/GO-ERR) — should the SDK's 12 typed exit-code errors be switched exhaustively, and at what FP cost on library code?

surprises: golangci-lint's default issues.uniq-by-line: true silently drops every same-line finding after the first — undocumented in the fetched docs, and it hid 4 of 22 planted MUST-linter violations in this dive's own fixture until explicitly set to false.

gosec's G101 (hardcoded credentials) only fires on package/file-scope const/var declarations — a functionally identical local `:=` credential assignment inside a function body produces zero findings, verified on a planted fixture.

exclusions.presets: [std-error-handling] silently exempts certain idiomatic error-drop patterns (e.g. os.Remove) from errcheck before nolint filtering runs, so a well-formed //nolint:errcheck next to such a call gets flagged by nolintlint as 'unused' — correct behavior, but confusing without knowing the preset acted first.

This dive's own attempt to reproduce 'golangci-lint's bundled staticcheck ignores a standalone staticcheck.conf' (the map's conflict 20, sourced from the wave-1 audit) was inconclusive: neither the bundled nor standalone staticcheck honored the planted conf file in this sandbox, likely due to the run.sh toolchain wrapper's working-directory handling — reported as a negative result rather than folded into a false claim.

bodyclose's only false-positive shape found in the corpus (100% of oras-go's 88 hits) is a response body wrapped into another io.ReadCloser-returning constructor and closed several calls removed from the http.Get site — a real, structural limitation of its static trace, not a general noise problem.

usestdlibvars's http-status-code check only fires on a typed comparison like resp.StatusCode == 200, not an arbitrary int == 200 — a scope caveat that cost real iteration time to discover empirically.

go fix's omitzero fixer is NOT unconditionally behavior-changing: for the common case (a zero-valued nested struct tagged omitempty) it silently applies the safe alternative (drop the no-op omitempty) and logs that it declined the risky rewrite — the map's blanket 'omitzero changes JSON output' claim only holds for a narrower case this dive did not need to construct.

golangci-lint's bundled govet linter is bit-for-bit equivalent to bare go vet on Go-1.25-era analyzers (hostport, waitgroup) when built against the same toolchain, meaning a golangci-lint-gated repo needs no separate go vet step at all — this simplifies the ordered command block for 2/3 of the corpus.

A tool directive's dependency footprint is NOT dev-only: a consumer importing a tool-carrying library inherits the tool's own transitive module requirements in its own go list -m all, even though the tool itself never becomes runnable via the consumer's go tool.

stdversion joining go test's default vet subset is itself brand-new in Go 1.27, not a long-standing behavior since 1.22 as an early draft of this dive assumed — a module on a pre-1.27 toolchain gets no stdversion protection from go test at all.
govulncheck's reachable-vulnerability exit code is 3, not 1 — an agent hand-authoring a CI gate from memory would likely guess the wrong non-zero value.

hostport's vet analyzer only fires when the Sprintf-built address string is consumed by net.Dial in the SAME function; splitting the Sprintf call into a helper function (an entirely reasonable refactor) silently defeats the analyzer, discovered only by watching a first fixture attempt pass vet cleanly when it should have failed.

rule_ids: GO-ERR-01 — Wrap with %w; never %v/%s an error; at a hiding boundary flatten with err.Error() under your own %w sentinel (MUST, errorlint errorf)
GO-ERR-02 — Match errors with errors.Is/As/AsType, never ==, type assertion or type switch (MUST, errorlint comparison+asserts; vet errorsas separately)
GO-ERR-03 — Return io.EOF unwrapped from every io.Reader implementation (MUST, reading heuristic; io.go:37-38)
GO-ERR-04 — Use errors.AsType in go>=1.26 modules (SHOULD, go fix -diff errorsastype; go vet stdversion guards the floor)
GO-ERR-05 — Never return a concrete *XxxError variable through an error result; helpers return error (MUST, SA4023 + reading heuristic for its _test.go blind spot)
GO-ERR-06 — Defer the returned cleanup: defer start()() (MUST, SA9010, staticcheck>=2026.2)
GO-ERR-07 — Lower-case, unpunctuated error strings without 'failed to'; %w last except a sentinel-category prefix (SHOULD, ST1005 + reading)
GO-ERR-08 — Check Close/Flush/Sync of writable resources via named-return defer errors.Join (MUST, errcheck without preset)
GO-ERR-09 — Exempt read-only closes only via exclude-functions (io.ReadCloser).Close; never enable the std-error-handling preset (MUST, grep config)
GO-ERR-10 — Recover only in a deferred func at a goroutine/API boundary and always use the value (SHOULD, errcheck partial + reading)
GO-ERR-11 — Never return nil after if err != nil (MUST, nilerr)
GO-ERR-12 — Signal absence with a sentinel/typed error or (v, ok); never (nil, nil) for pointer/iface/func or in-band -1/"" (SHOULD, nilnil with checked-types minus map)
GO-ERR-13 — Call os.Exit/log.Fatal* only from func main (and TestMain), never after a defer (MUST, revive deep-exit explicit + gocritic exitAfterDefer)
GO-ERR-14 — Never classify errors by err.Error() text (MUST, grep)
GO-ERR-15 — Panic in library/SDK code only for invariants or programmer misuse; no must()/try() over runtime values (MUST, grep + reading)
GO-ERR-16 — Never %w another module's error from an exported function unless the doc comment names it; translate to your own sentinel (MUST, reading heuristic)
GO-ERR-17 — Export sentinels for data-less conditions, pointer-receiver typed errors for data; one receiver kind per type everywhere (SHOULD, reading)
GO-ERR-18 — Walk Unwrap() []error when every joined match matters; As/AsType returns only the first (SHOULD, count-asserting test)
GO-ERR-19 — Handle each error once; deliberate discards are explicit _ = with a reason; check-blank stays off (SHOULD, reading)
GO-ERR-20 — OCX SDK: one *ExitError{Code}, a separate *TimeoutError never matching it, retry only on 75 (MUST for SDK, contract test)
conflicts_resolved: errorlint errorf vs Google's %v hiding idiom (map conflict 22's nolint vs the wrap dive's Contested section): errorf stays on and boundaries flatten with err.Error() under %s; watched boundary_twin show 0 issues and its test pass
errorf off by default (standalone go-errorlint, per the map) vs on (golangci-lint 2.14.0 once errorlint is enabled): both are true; re-run confirmed
the errorlint io.EOF blind spot is not a linter gap: io.EOF's doc requires Read to return it unwrapped, so the defect is in the reader (new GO-ERR-03)
map M-B-04 treats errorlint and vet errorsas as one check: they are two axes and both run
ST1005 'divergence' under golangci-lint is uniq-by-line dedup, not a gap (re-run with --uniq-by-line=false)
SA4023 blind spot for test-only comparisons confirmed by re-run (-tests=true, exit 0), so GO-ERR-05 also needs a reading heuristic
pec dive's advice to set uniq-by-line false is rejected: deep-exit and exitAfterDefer overlap only where either suffices (verified on exitmain)
exits banned outside 'package main' (map) vs outside 'func main' (revive deep-exit): the stricter form wins, matching EXIT-02; verified helpers are flagged and TestMain is exempt

the claim that 'defer resp.Body.Close() is an accepted idiom' (runtime audit) fails because errcheck v2 has no default exclusion: exempt read-only closes only with (io.ReadCloser).Close and forbid the std-error-handling preset
nilnil flags nil-map returns, which the pec dive calls fine: checked-types is tuned to drop map (verified 2 issues by default, 1 tuned)
(nil, nil) contested in the map: kept at SHOULD because no Go-team normative source supports a MUST

typed-error receiver kind (map conflict 7 says pointer; cli/cli uses a value receiver for a marker): pointer is the default and a value receiver is allowed only for data-less markers matched consistently
one SDK *ExitError with a Code field, not 12 per-code types as in ocx-sdk-python (Go has no exhaustive match)
wrapcheck is not adopted (about 65-75% false positives on a grpc-go sample)
pec dive says trivy has no std-error-handling preset: wrong, trivy@ae561f8cca36:.golangci.yaml:201 enables it
panic counts 4,236 vs 4,355 differ only by denominator; rules cite 4,236
exit_code.rs citation corrected from 27-38 to 32-46 at ocx@2691d3c1638e
errorlint vs the <=1 FP/10k LOC MUST bar: admitted on a 0/15 FP spot-read, with the sample size flagged for re-measurement
needs_another_round: gates/golangci-config: what is errorlint's per-10k-LOC false-positive rate on >=5 exemplars (caddy's 462 hits were never spot-read), re-measured after rewriting hiding boundaries to the err.Error() idiom?
sdk/sdk-surface: what does *ExitError carry beyond Code (raw Stderr vs the decoded CLI-04 JSON error envelope), and does the envelope's stable slug become a field?
errors/sa4023-upstream: is SA4023's test-file blind spot intentional or a bug in dominikh/go-tools? A fix would collapse GO-ERR-05 to SA4023 alone

surprises: A module declaring `go 1.25` compiles fine calling `errors.AsType` (a 1.26 stdlib API) on a 1.27.1 toolchain — stdlib API availability isn't gated by the module's go line the way language builtins are; the real, catchable hazard is go vet's stdversion analyzer, and staticcheck does NOT catch it at all (verified both ways).

errorlint's errorf check flags the exact Google-best-practices-sanctioned boundary pattern (%w for an own sentinel + %v for a leaked dependency detail in the same fmt.Errorf call) as a violation — the linter can't distinguish deliberate opacity from omission.

staticcheck's SA4023 has a verified, reproducible blind spot: it never fires when the only nil-comparison of a typed-nil-returned-as-error bug lives in a _test.go file, even though it fires reliably on the identical code in a .go file (confirmed with 4 fixture variants).

errorlint's io.EOF/sql.ErrNoRows exemption is keyed to the call's *static* interface type, not the concrete implementation — a hand-rolled io.Reader that silently wraps EOF defeats the exemption entirely and is never flagged, even though the == comparison genuinely breaks.

wrapcheck flags a decorator method's bare passthrough of the identical interface method it implements (e.g. a wrapping ClientStream delegating SendMsg/RecvMsg) as an 'unwrapped external error' — a structural false-positive class distinct from ordinary noise.

cli/cli's own error-type file uses both a pointer-receiver-with-Unwrap type (FlagError) and a plain value-receiver type with no Unwrap (NoResultsError) side by side, correctly — 'always pointer receiver' is an oversimplification of real, sanctioned practice.

golangci-lint v2.14.0 has ZERO default exclusions (v1's silent EXC0001 suppression of unchecked .*Close/.*Flush/os.Remove errcheck findings is gone) — verified empirically before finding the primary source confirming it.

The `std-error-handling` preset that restores the old 'accepted defer resp.Body.Close()' behavior is read/write-blind: enabling it also silences the exact write-close defect (unchecked f.Close on an os.Create handle) this whole subarea exists to catch.

revive's `deep-exit` rule is NOT in golangci-lint v2.14.0's default revive rule set — it only fires with an explicit `revive.settings.rules: [{name: deep-exit}]` entry, contrary to the assumption that enabling `revive` covers it.

golangci-lint's default `issues.uniq-by-line: true` silently drops one of two findings when revive's deep-exit and go-critic's exitAfterDefer both fire on the same os.Exit/log.Fatal line — enabling both gives no more coverage than either alone unless uniq-by-line is disabled.

gosec's G104 is documented in golangci-lint's own source as 'Duplicated errcheck checks' and never fired in any run against several unchecked-error fixtures — it is not a second line of defense, contrary to how it reads in gosec's own rule catalogue.

A 40-site stratified sample of a naive `_ =` grep found ~1/3 (13/40) were not error discards at all: stringer-generated `_ = x[Const-N]` bounds-check idiom and protobuf's `_ = protoimpl.EnforceVersion(...)` marker — naive counts of 'discarded errors' massively overstate the real surface.

rule_ids: GO-CONC-01 — Take ctx first, propagate it to every callee, never restart with Background()/TODO() below an entrypoint, never ship TODO() in library code, never pass nil (contextcheck + revive context-as-argument + SA1012; MUST)
GO-CONC-02 — Never store a context in a struct field or accept it via a functional option; owner types store cancel + done; retrofit exception only with //nolint:containedctx (containedctx; MUST)
GO-CONC-03 — Call the context-taking form of exec, http and net calls, tests included (noctx; MUST)
GO-CONC-04 — Key context.WithValue with an unexported package type and use Value only for request-scoped cross-boundary data (SA1029; MUST on key type)
GO-CONC-05 — Never reassign ctx = With*(ctx, ...) inside a loop or repeated closure (fatcontext; SHOULD)
GO-CONC-06 — Call every cancel func on every path via an immediate defer; comment a stored cancel with its owner (go vet lostcancel; MUST)
GO-CONC-07 — Use wg.Go at go>=1.25, otherwise call wg.Add before the go statement, never inside it (vet waitgroup, Go 1.25; MUST)
GO-CONC-08 — Never copy a Mutex/RWMutex/WaitGroup/Once/Cond after first use (go vet copylocks; MUST)
GO-CONC-09 — Allow one writer per goroutine-written variable, read only after the join; guard anything multi-writer, never share append/map/err (go test -race; MUST)
GO-CONC-10 — Give every goroutine an owner with a reachable join or a documented Close/Shutdown (reading heuristic, justified; MUST)
GO-CONC-11 — Call goleak.VerifyTestMain in every package that starts goroutines; do not use synctest as a leak detector (MUST for SDK and libraries, SHOULD for CLIs)
GO-CONC-12 — Use typed atomics, not the atomic.AddInt64 family or go.uber.org/atomic (go fix -diff atomictypes; SHOULD)
GO-CONC-13 — Bound every fan-out sized by input, wire or arguments with SetLimit, TryGo or a semaphore (reading heuristic, justified; MUST)
GO-CONC-14 — Choose WaitGroup.Go for infallible tasks, errgroup+SetLimit for fail-fast, a collector + errors.Join for report-all commands (SHOULD)
GO-CONC-15 — Close a channel once, from the sole sender after a barrier; buffers are 0 or 1 unless justified (SHOULD)
GO-CONC-16 — Do not blanket-recover in library goroutines; recover and report with the stack only around foreign callbacks or at daemon-loop tops (SHOULD)

GO-CONC-17 — Attach a cause where the cancellation reason must reach a caller (SDK WithTimeoutCause); take CLI exit status from a typed signal.Notify channel, with NotifyContext only for propagation (SHOULD)
GO-CONC-18 — Use sync.OnceValue/OnceValues for fallible lazy init and never memoize transient failures (SHOULD)
GO-CONC-19 — Detach outliving work with WithoutCancel and replace Done-waiting goroutines with AfterFunc, calling stop (CONSIDER)
conflicts_resolved: vet waitgroup analyzer version: goroutine-ownership said Go 1.27, gate-commands said 1.25; resolved to 1.25 per the go1.25 release notes

NotifyContext cause as the CLI exit path: context-contract rule 6 vs exit-codes-and-signals §7 (the cause is an unexported string); CLI exit status comes from a typed signal.Notify channel, NotifyContext is for propagation only

Library goroutine recover: goroutine-ownership rule 5 'always recover and report' vs errgroup's rationale, GO-ERR's panic policy and panics-exits-cleanup rule 9; no blanket recover, only around foreign callbacks and at daemon-loop tops
ctx-first verification: context-contract cited contextcheck, which checks chains, not position; position is revive context-as-argument, watched red [C-1]
Closure writes to an outer var: 'never a bare shared variable' vs trivy's correct wg.Go single-writer; single writer + read after the join is allowed, multi-writer must be guarded
contextcheck MUST-eligibility: measured on the 8 gate repos [C-3], 6/8 at <=1 FP/10k LOC; urfave/cli's 152 hits are one TODO() root amplified
noctx scope: exec+http only vs the measured net.Dial/Listen/LookupIP coverage, with 71/91 hits in tests; the rule covers the net family and includes tests (fix is t.Context())
etcd citation: context-contract cited session.go:120 as the Session struct; :120 is sessionOptions.ctx (a WithContext option) and Session.ctx is :35; the options idiom is banned for the SDK
goleak vs owner Q2 (go-cmp the only test dep): default admits goleak as a second test-only dependency, flagged as an owner question
needs_another_round: concurrency/leak-detection-stdlib — Does a TestMain runtime.Stack baseline diff match goleak's 3/3 on the planted leaks, and is the goroutineleak profile usable in tests at the SDK's go 1.26.0 floor?
concurrency/report-all-fanout (M-C-04) — Plant errgroup vs WaitGroup+errors.Join on a 3-failure batch and record which errors reach the caller, to watch GO-CONC-14 red
concurrency/fanout-analyzer — Is a small go/analysis pass (range + .Go/go with no SetLimit/semaphore in scope) worth shipping to mechanize GO-CONC-13? Measure it on the 94 triage sites
testing x concurrency — Does any analyzer catch t.FailNow inside wg.Go/errgroup.Go closures (vet testinggoroutine covers bare go only, unverified)?

surprises: testing/synctest.Test's own deadlock detector only catches a leak whose blocking channel was created inside the bubble; a goroutine blocked on real I/O or on a channel created outside the bubble (e.g. a package-level var) doesn't fail cleanly — it HANGS until go test's own -timeout kills it with 'panic: test timed out'.

The go1.27 goroutineleak profile's blind spot on a goroutine blocked via a reachable package-level global is not just plausible — the Go 1.27 release notes state it explicitly ('may fail to identify leaks... reachable through global variables'), and this dive's own fixture independently reproduced exactly that miss.

go vet's `waitgroup` analyzer (misplaced wg.Add) is completely invisible to `go test -race`, even at -count=10 — it's a logical/ordering bug, not a memory race the detector's model covers, despite Uber's PLDI'22 paper attributing 24 real production races to this exact shape.

-race catches 'send on closed channel' as a genuine DATA RACE only intermittently (1 of 5 runs in this dive) — the other 4 runs simply hit the deterministic runtime panic with no race report at all, so a single green -race run proves nothing about this ordering bug.

Reading errgroup's own source comment reveals it deliberately does NOT propagate panics to Wait() and cites four separate golang/go issues explaining why that would be worse — a documented design stance, not an oversight, contradicting an intuitive assumption that errgroup is a panic-safety boundary.

A variable named `wg` is not reliable evidence it's a sync.WaitGroup — cli/cli's own exemplar code declares `var wg errgroup.Group` and calls `wg.Go(func() error {...})`, structurally impossible for sync.WaitGroup.Go; any grep-based heuristic must check the declaration, not the identifier.

contextcheck produced a confirmed false positive on the deliberate functional-options-override-context idiom at google/go-containerregistry@0c8bedb78437:pkg/v1/remote/catalog.go:75 — a MUST-backing linter still needs a documented per-site suppression path for this shape

staticcheck SA1012 (nil context) did not fire when nil was passed through a func(context.Context) error indirection — it only catches the direct-literal-argument shape, a real detection gap worth flagging to the map's other rows

No analyzer in the golangci-lint 2.14.0 set (govet, staticcheck, contextcheck, containedctx, noctx, fatcontext) catches WithTimeout losing its cause vs WithTimeoutCause — confirmed by running the full set against a planted violation and getting 0 issues; this is reading-heuristic-only, contrary to what one might assume given how many context-specific linters exist
signal.NotifyContext's cancellation-cause behavior is a Go 1.26 change to an *existing* function's semantics, not a new function — code on go 1.25 or lower silently lacks it with no compiler warning

fatcontext and SA1029/nil-context patterns produced zero live hits across the three measured exemplars (etcd, cli/cli, go-containerregistry) despite firing correctly on fixtures — both rules are real but rare in mature corpora, so their exemplar evidence is fixture-only

noctx's os/exec.Command coverage flagged a legitimate zero-context use (cli/cli's own build script run() helper) that has no caller to cancel it — the rule's reading heuristic must carve out build-tooling scripts, not just test files

rule_ids: GO-TEST-01 — Call t.Fatal/FailNow/Skip*/require.* only from the test goroutine; run go vet explicitly (testinggoroutine is not in go test's subset); treat FailNow in wg.Go/errgroup.Go closures as a reading heuristic, since neither vet nor testifylint sees it (MUST)
GO-TEST-02 — Write new tests with stdlib testing plus go-cmp (got/want, cmp.Diff with (-want +got)); never introduce testify; enforce with a depguard no-testify rule on $test files (MUST)
GO-TEST-03 — In a repo already standardized on testify, keep it, enable testifylint at defaults and use require for preconditions (MUST, testify repos only)
GO-TEST-04 — Do not import both testify and go-cmp into one test package (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-05 — Start every test helper with t.Helper(); never build a private assertion library (thelper) (MUST)
GO-TEST-06 — At go>=1.24 use t.Context/TempDir/Setenv/Chdir/Cleanup; enforce with usetesting (context-background and context-todo set true) plus go fix -diff testingcontext (MUST)
GO-TEST-07 — Shape table tests as a keyed slice of structs with named t.Run subtests and no tt := tt copy at go>=1.22 (go fix forvar / copyloopvar) (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-08 — Test HTTP code against httptest (and ggcr registry.New for OCI); mock only non-HTTP seams with go.uber.org/mock; never import github.com/golang/mock (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-09 — Give parallel tests their own fixtures and prove them under go test -race; never back this with paralleltest or tparallel (MUST)
GO-TEST-10 — Give cmp.Diff explicit options (IgnoreUnexported, EquateEmpty, EquateErrors); never change production returns to satisfy a test (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-11 — At go>=1.25 test time-dependent concurrent code inside synctest.Test; never write synctest.Run (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-12 — Test CLI wrappers with a TestMain re-exec helper process covering every exit code; never exec the real binary in unit tests (MUST for the SDK, SHOULD for CLIs)
GO-TEST-13 — Keep golden files under testdata with one -update flag and deterministic comparison; a missing golden file fails the test (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-14 — Give every untrusted-input parser a FuzzXxx target with edge-case f.Add seeds and commit failures under testdata/fuzz (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-15 — Bound every CI fuzz invocation with -fuzztime (MUST)
GO-TEST-16 — Gate coverage with a fail-closed script over the go tool cover -func total line, run from the module root; no -fail-under flag exists (MUST for the SDK at 100%)
GO-TEST-17 — Collect integration coverage with go build -cover and GOCOVERDIR, and fail the harness when the coverage directory is empty (MUST where claimed)
GO-TEST-18 — Test CLIs in-process through run(args, stdin, stdout, stderr) and add testscript .txtar suites for multi-step and real-argv behaviour (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-19 — Use b.Loop for new benchmarks; rewrite b.N benchmarks only by hand with benchstat; never call b.Loop with the timer stopped (SHOULD)
GO-TEST-20 — Back every performance claim with benchstat over -count=10 runs and a p-value (MUST, reading heuristic)
conflicts_resolved: C1: test-style claimed testinggoroutine is part of go test. It is not (go1.27.1 test.go:684 is commented out); go test exits 0 and go vet exits 1 on the same fixture, so GO-TEST-01 needs an explicit vet step.

C2: test-style (quoting the testifylint README) said go-require catches require inside wg.Go. In testifylint v1.6.4 / golangci-lint 2.14.0 it does not, and vet also misses t.Fatal in wg.Go (watched), so that case is a reading heuristic.
C3: test-style said no go fix fixer exists for tt := tt. go fix -diff (forvar) and copyloopvar both flag it (watched red and green); the dive's line-anchored grep missed a commented copy.

C4: time-fuzz-coverage said usetesting os-setenv defaults to false. It defaults to true in golangci-lint 2.14.0 (reference.yml:4230-4232; the default config flagged os.Setenv); only context-background and context-todo need enabling.

C5: test-style said no exemplar package mixes testify and go-cmp. Measured per file: etcd 14, containerd 6, cosign 1 (e.g. etcd demux_test.go:21-22). GO-TEST-04 is kept as a fleet SHOULD, with those repos listed as violating.
C6: time-fuzz-coverage said any StopTimer/StartTimer breaks b.Loop. On 1.27.1 only calling b.Loop with the timer stopped fails (benchmark.go:417); a Stop-then-Start pair inside the body passes.

C7: time-fuzz-coverage said an empty profile gives exit 2. An empty profile reports 0.0% and exits 1; exit 2 comes from running outside the module root. Both fail closed, and the rule now requires running from the module root.
C8: test-style proposed MUST for EquateEmpty/IgnoreUnexported. Demoted to SHOULD: the panic self-reports and nil-vs-empty intent is only a reading heuristic.
C9: the shifts scout's testify-v1 default is rejected under map conflict 1; this consolidation adds the depguard enforcement and the testifylint tolerance mechanism.
C10: paralleltest/tparallel are noise (2,357 to 2,557 hits on clean repos); races are proven by -race, and a planted race passes plain go test.

Map rows: M-E-17 dropped because go test already fails on malformed test names (the vet tests analyzer is in the default subset; watched); M-E-14 dropped; M-E-12 routed to docs-instrument; M-E-11 owned by GO-GATE-COMMANDS-08.

surprises: A single unsynchronized x++ across two t.Parallel subtests often passes -race by luck; only a wide race window (200k-iteration loops behind a shared start signal) made detection reliable (3/3 runs) — a naive one-line race fixture would be flaky as a verification.

google/go-github already uses testing/synctest.Test (Go 1.25 GA) in its own test suite (github_test.go:3236,3288) — live confirmation of a shift the topic map's shifts scout only argued from release notes.

testifylint is dramatically more useful as a signal on a testify-heavy repo (1,485 real findings on cli/cli, dominated by require-error) than golangci-lint's other test linters — it does not belong in the same 'noise' bucket as paralleltest/tparallel.

goreleaser is 97% require-disciplined already (6,563 require calls vs 173 assert calls in its own tests) — its testify usage is closer to the fleet's tolerance clause than to the naive 'testify = sloppy' assumption.

cli/cli ships both CLI-testing shapes (in-process ghcmd.Main() and testscript.RunMain-driven acceptance tests) in the same repo, confirming they are complementary rather than a style choice to pick once.
golang/mock has zero remaining importers anywhere in the 34-repo exemplar corpus — the archival is not just documented, it's already fully absorbed in practice.

b.Loop() was +182.86% slower than b.N for an identical 100-int-sum benchmark body (p=0.002, n=6) -- far worse than the +65% figure cited in golang/go#74967, showing bloop's overhead can dominate at nanosecond scale even more than the Go team's own cautionary example

usetesting's most valuable checks (os-setenv, context-background, context-todo) default to false in the linter itself -- 'enable usetesting' in a golangci-lint config is not sufficient by itself and needs explicit settings overrides
the planted fuzz target's own seed corpus (not generative fuzzing) already reproduced the panic -- go test's default seed-corpus run is a real, cheap safety net independent of whether -fuzz ever runs

go fix's modernizer suite as of 1.27.1 has no bloop fixer at all -- it was proposed, shipped, then deliberately removed after golang/go#74967, so 'go fix modernizes b.N to b.Loop automatically' is false for the current toolchain
CI actually running go test -fuzz is only 3/32 workflow-bearing exemplars, far below what the fuzz-function count (122) would suggest
no exemplar in the 35-repo corpus runs benchstat in CI at all (0/32), despite it being the Go team's own documented answer to benchmark noise

rule_ids: GO-MOD-01 — Libraries and the SDK declare go 1.26.0 (the oldest supported release's .0, or lower); CLIs declare go 1.27.0; never leave init's patch-level line in a library
GO-MOD-02 — Never write a toolchain line in a library or SDK; a CLI carries exactly one, toolchain go1.27.N (latest patch, above the go line), set with go get toolchain@
GO-MOD-03 — Commit go.sum, gate CI on go mod tidy -diff, keep -mod=readonly, never set -mod=mod in CI
GO-MOD-04 — Name only live godebug settings in go.mod (a removed one only at its final value); pin compatibility with the godebug line, not a GODEBUG env var
GO-MOD-05 — Commit go.work only in a multi-module repo, and build and test every member module from its own root with GOWORK=off
GO-MOD-06 — Run every repo-wide gate once per go.mod root, never a single root ./...
GO-MOD-07 — Keep replace out of library and SDK go.mod; allow only local-path replaces in monorepos; never fix a CVE or bug with replace

GO-MOD-08 — Deny superseded modules through one shared depguard 'superseded' rule (pkg/errors, xerrors, io/ioutil, x/exp/slices and maps, golang/mock, gopkg.in/yaml.v2 and v3, ghodss/yaml, satori uuid, go-multierror)
GO-MOD-09 — Apply go-line-gated supersessions only above their floor: google/uuid to stdlib uuid at go>=1.27 for New/Parse-only use; delete automaxprocs at main-module go>=1.25
GO-MOD-10 — Keep the SDK's runtime import graph stdlib-only, checked with go list -deps on .Module.Main (test-only go-cmp allowed)
GO-MOD-11 — Put no tool directive in the SDK or a library; pin their dev tools in the workflow
GO-MOD-12 — Run govulncheck ./... in text mode as a blocking step per module; a traced finding blocks and is fixed by upgrade, never replace; an untraced one is scheduled
GO-MOD-13 — Audit the exact release artifact and mirrored upstream binaries with govulncheck -mode=binary as a second gate, expecting over-reporting on stripped builds
GO-MOD-14 — Add the /vN suffix to the module line and self-imports with the first v2+ tag; never commit +incompatible; tag nested modules dir/vX.Y.Z
GO-MOD-15 — Fix a bad tag with retract plus a reason comment in a new, higher tag; never delete or re-tag

GO-MOD-16 — Select Go in CI so shipped binaries get the latest patch: libraries use [oldstable, stable], CLIs use go-version-file reading the toolchain line, never go-version-file on a bare go 1.N.0 line for release builds; set GOTOOLCHAIN=local
GO-MOD-17 — Configure a grouped Dependabot gomod block and have a human review every bump
GO-MOD-18 — Set GOPRIVATE for private-module jobs and never set GOAUTH=off (CONSIDER)
conflicts_resolved: toolchain line: the dives say avoid it (5/35 minority), Q1 allows it for a security patch -> libraries never carry one; CLIs carry toolchain go1.27.N as the patch pin CI reads (cli/cli and etcd pattern)

GOWORK=off in CI: the directives dive says never; go.dev/ref/mod says CI should not use go.work -> each member must build with GOWORK=off (run C4: a use-only sibling is red, replaced or published is green); prometheus, etcd and k8s comply
SDK zero-dependency check: dependency-hygiene claimed go list -deps includes test imports and filtered only the exact module path -> both wrong (run C8); replaced with a .Module.Main template

check-latest and go-version-file: the directives dive says go-version-file everywhere and check-latest on release jobs only; dependency-hygiene says check-latest everywhere -> setup-go docs say a patch-level go line installs that exact patch and check-latest cannot fix it; resolved as GO-MOD-16 (aliases for libraries, toolchain-line go-version-file for CLIs)

go.work.sum: the directives dive requires it always and flags prometheus -> go.dev says it is written only for extra hashes, and C4's workspace build wrote none; commit it when it exists, prometheus is compliant

M-L-03 premise (go mod init writes N-1): the map took it from the go1.26 notes -> reverted in 1.26.1 (golang/go#77653, #77860), and 1.27.1 writes go 1.27.1; GO-MOD-01 requires lowering it for libraries
Blanket golang.org/x/exp deny: dependency-hygiene denied the whole module -> deny only x/exp/slices and x/exp/maps, since x/exp ships ungraduated packages (apidiff, mmap, ebnf)
Ownership of M-L-04 and M-L-09: gate-commands wrote them as GO-GATE-COMMANDS-05 and -10 -> the map assigns section L to GO-MOD, so GO-MOD-03 and GO-MOD-11 own them and GO-GATE cites them
needs_another_round: dependency-hygiene / Dependabot and toolchain: does Dependabot's gomod ecosystem open PRs for the toolchain directive and go-line bumps, and how does grouping interact (decides whether GO-MOD-16's patch cadence needs a skill step)?

dependency-hygiene / govulncheck binary mode: is -mode=binary over-reporting on -s -w builds documented, and what does it find on the four mirrored bazelbuild binaries (bazelisk, buildifier, buildozer, unused-deps)?

directives / go.work godebug and ignore: which wins, a go.work godebug (kubernetes go.work:5) or a member's go.mod godebug under GOWORK=off, and should fleet repos adopt the 1.25 ignore directive for docs and asset trees?
directives / nested-module tagging: plant a nested module behind a local proxy to prove dir/vX.Y.Z tag resolution, so GO-MOD-14 gains a run instead of a reading heuristic

surprises: go mod init on Go 1.27.1 writes go 1.27.1 (current version), not go 1.26.0 (N-1) — the Go-1.26.0-only default was reverted in 1.26.1 per golang/go#77653 and #77860, overturning the topic map's M-L-03 framing which was sourced only from the go1.26 release notes

A two-module go.work repo's use-only sibling dependency (no replace) fails hard under GOWORK=off with a missing go.sum entry, and go mod tidy under GOWORK=off cannot even repair it because the dependency has no real fetchable path — this is why go.work CI must never disable the workspace for a whole-tree build

A nested module's packages are completely invisible to go list ./... run from the parent module root — not partially, not with a warning — which means any repo-wide gate that assumes one ./... invocation covers a monorepo silently skips every nested module (kubernetes ~34, plus etcd, terraform, trivy)
prometheus/prometheus commits go.work but not go.work.sum, breaking the '3/4 commit both' pattern the rest of the corpus follows

GOTOOLCHAIN=auto on a version the network can't supply fails with 'toolchain not available' rather than falling back — the failure mode is identical in shape to what a network-isolated CI runner hits on a routine dependency bump, not just on a deliberately-too-new fixture

grpc/grpc-go has never done a breaking major-version bump and stays unsuffixed at v1.8x by design, while google/go-github bumps on every breaking change and sits at /v92 — both are live, opposite, equally valid strategies with no ecosystem convergence

govulncheck -mode=binary on a -s -w stripped binary reports 4x more vulnerabilities with no call-graph narrowing (falls back to a flat 'vulnerable symbols found' list) than the identical unstripped binary — stripping a release binary makes its own govulncheck audit less precise, not more secure.

govulncheck-action's -format json/-format sarif ALWAYS exits 0 regardless of findings; only the default text format fails the job — a CI step piping to JSON for a dashboard is decorative unless it adds its own exit-code check.

A stdlib `uuid` package genuinely ships in Go 1.27.1 (confirmed by reading GOROOT/src/uuid/uuid.go directly) but its surface is much narrower than github.com/google/uuid — no NewV6, NewSHA1, NewMD5, NewDCE*, Validate, or ParseBytes — so 'migrate to stdlib uuid' is wrong advice for any caller using those.

go-yaml/yaml (the upstream gopkg.in/yaml.v2/v3 has pointed at for years) was archived by its maintainer on 2025-04-01, and go.yaml.in/yaml — the community successor — already has more direct adopters (9/35) than the old gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (5/35) in the exemplar corpus, ahead of where a cautious rule-writer would expect.

Two exemplars (uber-go/zap, kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime) have a dependabot.yml that covers github-actions only, with zero gomod block — file presence is not evidence Go dependency updates are automated at all.

golang/mock is confirmed archived (archived:true, pushed_at 2024-01-08) via direct GitHub API query, and its successor go.uber.org/mock is confirmed live and unarchived — worth stating definitively rather than hedging.

rule_ids: GO-CLI-01 — Declare one type ExitCode int holding the fleet table (0,1,64,65,69,74,75,77,78,79,80,81; SDK adds ocx 82-86), name constants ExitXxx, pass only int(code) to os.Exit, and check every switch over it with exhaustive
GO-CLI-02 — Make main exactly run/reraise/os.Exit and keep every defer, flush and signal.Stop in run; nothing else calls os.Exit, log.Fatal* or cobra.CheckErr
GO-CLI-03 — Write results only to a writer injected from run; forbid fmt.Print*/print/println via forbidigo and parse all of stdout in a JSON-mode test
GO-CLI-04 — Buffer output in one bufio.Writer created in run and errors.Join its Flush error into the classified error; never defer w.Flush() with the error dropped
GO-CLI-05 — Classify errors in one ordered classify(err) chain (broken pipe, signal, typed via errors.AsType, not-started to 64, fall-through 1) locked by one real-invocation test per code
GO-CLI-06 — Set SilenceErrors/SilenceUsage on the cobra root and wrap every RunE once so any untyped error before a RunE ran exits 64
GO-CLI-07 — Notify SIGPIPE at the top of run and map a broken pipe to exit 0 only in classify via a per-OS isBrokenPipe (EPIPE; Windows ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE/Errno 232)
GO-CLI-08 — Derive SIGINT/SIGTERM status from a typed WithCancelCause SignalError and re-raise the signal on Unix; never hardcode 130 or parse NotifyContext's cause string
GO-CLI-09 — Prompt only when stdin is a TTY with a --yes bypass (else return UsageError), and never take secrets from flag values or plain env vars
GO-CLI-10 — Make mutating subcommands safe to re-run after a crash by staging and committing atomically and idempotently
GO-CLI-11 — Render the error chain once in run to stderr through a named sanitize stripping C0/C1 controls and unicode.Bidi_Control runes
GO-CLI-12 — Never forward exec.ExitError.ExitCode() unchecked; map a Signaled() WaitStatus to 128+N
GO-CLI-13 — Decide colour per stream in one module: --color, NO_COLOR non-empty, TERM=dumb, IsTerminal||IsCygwinTerminal per fd; never LookupEnv(NO_COLOR) or fatih/color's global
GO-CLI-14 — Take config/cache dirs from os.UserConfigDir/UserCacheDir, never a HOME/USERPROFILE join, and prefix every tool env var
GO-CLI-15 — Apply flags > env > project > user > system as an explicit layer walk and do not add viper without a remote-provider or hot-reload need
GO-CLI-16 — Build multi-command CLIs on cobra+pflag and single-command tools on stdlib flag; do not adopt urfave/cli v3
conflicts_resolved: Cobra exit-64 wiring: exit dive's SetFlagErrorFunc+wrapArgs misses unknown-subcommand and required-flag errors (verified exit 1); streams dive's 'every Execute error -> 64' misclassifies business errors. Resolved: Silence* plus a RunE-started phase marker (verified 64 on all four usage classes, 1 on RunE error).
Streams dive and config-inventory §4 claim cobra calls os.Exit(1) by default; cobra Execute never exits (command.go:1070-1073). Corrected.
Both dives claimed no linter covers defer-skipped-by-os.Exit; gocritic exitAfterDefer flags it (watched red/green) and errcheck flags a dropped defer w.Flush().
Flush discipline: streams dive's 'explicit Flush before every os.Exit' replaced by the exit dive's two-line main plus a classified Flush error (verified >/dev/full 0 vs 74).

Signal status: exit dive's os.Exit(128+N) vs Rust EXIT-11 re-raise vs GO-CONC's reliance on NotifyContext's cause. Resolved: a typed WithCancelCause cause and a Unix re-raise (verified Python returncode 130 vs -2); NotifyContext's cause only for messages.
ExitCode naming: the exit dive's const UsageError collides with type UsageError; adopted GO-ERR's ExitXxx constant prefix.
Exit table scope: Rust rule table (to 82) vs ocx exit_code.rs (to 86) vs grimoire (to 81). Resolved: CLIs share core 0-81, and the SDK mirrors ocx's full 0-86.
SIGPIPE on Windows: EPIPE never matches there (source-read; cli/cli epipe_windows.go uses Errno 232). Resolved with a per-OS isBrokenPipe.
Exit dive said no exemplar uses SetFlagErrorFunc; trivy and cli/cli do.
Exit dive said WaitStatus mapping is Unix-only; it compiles on windows/darwin (Signaled() false), so no build tag is needed.
revive deep-exit does not flag cobra.CheckErr (watched); added a grep.
needs_another_round: cli/windows — watch GO-CLI-07 (ERROR_NO_DATA vs ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE on console vs pipe), GO-CLI-08 (Ctrl-C/Ctrl-Break delivery, exit status) and GO-CLI-13 (MSYS2 detection) go red/green on a windows-latest runner; only cross-compilation was verified

cli/reference-skeleton — does the markStarted RunE phase marker survive cobra TraverseChildren, aliases, __complete, and a runnable root with Args set before it ships as the support-directory example?
cli/colour-library — is there a per-stream colour library (termenv/lipgloss NewOutput(w)) satisfying GO-CLI-13 without a wrapper? Only fatih/color was surveyed

surprises: Cobra never calls os.Exit and never distinguishes usage errors by exit code at all — the '64 for bad flags' expectation is entirely on the CLI author to wire, and cobra provides a typed hook (SetFlagErrorFunc) for flag-parse errors only, not for arg-count or unknown-subcommand errors.

Setting a custom Args validator on cobra's root command silently disables cobra's own unknown-subcommand detection (legacyArgs only runs when Args is nil) — a mistyped subcommand then falls through to RunE as an ordinary positional argument instead of producing a usage error.

os/signal.NotifyContext's Go 1.26 'cause describing the signal' is not a typed value — the concrete type is an unexported string with no signal accessor, so the release-note wording is a plausible but false read of a typed API existing; only Error()-string-matching or a separate signal.Notify channel actually recovers the signal.
signal.Ignore(SIGPIPE) without an error check at the write site doesn't fail silently or safely — it panics to exit 2, which is worse than Go's unhandled default of dying to the signal itself (141).

os.Exit skipping deferred cleanup produces identical exit codes on the broken and fixed versions (both 0) — the bug is invisible to exit-code testing and shows up only in output content (a dropped buffered write), which is a real trap for exit-code-focused verification.

Trusting exec.ExitError.ExitCode() on a signal-killed child doesn't crash or obviously misbehave — it silently reports exit 255 instead of the correct 143, which would pass casual testing since only signal deaths (not ordinary failures) trigger the -1-to-255 truncation.

fmt's %q verb incidentally sanitizes CWE-150-relevant control/bidi-override characters via strconv.Quote's unicode.IsPrint check — the first fixture draft using %q as the 'violation' came out already escaped, forcing a redesign around %s.

urfave/cli v3.13.0 hardcodes exit code 3 (not a caller-configurable value) for an unrecognized subcommand via its help-fallback path, silently overriding a caller's own ExitCoder-based exit-64 convention unless CommandNotFound is set.

urfave/cli v3's own official exit-codes documentation example ends with log.Fatal(err), which always exits 1 and discards the cli.Exit(msg, 86) code the example just built — copying the framework's own docs verbatim breaks custom exit codes.

urfave/cli v3.13.0 produces the LARGEST binary of the three frameworks measured (3.55 MiB vs cobra's 2.43 MiB and stdlib flag's 1.52 MiB), contradicting an assumption that a minimal third-party CLI framework would be lighter than a batteries-included one like cobra.
A trivial one-line viper usage links to 5.19 MB and 47 go.sum entries — over 2x the size of koanf's equivalent (2.07 MB, 12 entries) and over 3x a full 5-subcommand stdlib-flag CLI (1.52 MB).

Even fatih/color (trivy's colour dependency, v1.19.0), which correctly implements NO_COLOR's non-emptiness check, computes its NoColor decision once as a package global against os.Stdout only — wrong the moment stdout and stderr have different TTY status.

rule_ids: GO-IO-01 — Start every child with exec.CommandContext; never exec.Command (noctx) [MUST]
GO-IO-02 — Open every externally-derived file name through os.Root; archive entries: reject !IsLocal first, never filepath.Join(dest, name) (gosec G305) [MUST]
GO-IO-03 — Bound every decompression with io.LimitReader plus declared-size and entry-count caps (gosec G110) [MUST]
GO-IO-04 — Never request 0o777/0o666; gate with gosec G301/G302/G306 at fleet thresholds 0755/0644, secrets 0600 [MUST]
GO-IO-05 — Binaries parsing tar/zip pin tarinsecurepath=0 and zipinsecurepath=0 in a go.mod godebug block; never execerrdot=0 (go list DefaultGODEBUG) [MUST]
GO-IO-06 — Keep Setpgid/Pdeathsig/syscall.Kill in unix-constrained files (GOOS=windows go vet ./...) [MUST]
GO-IO-07 — Set a nonzero Cmd.WaitDelay on every exec.Cmd; it is the kill grace after Cancel (grep) [MUST]
GO-IO-08 — Pass argv directly; never sh -c/bash -c/cmd /c (grep; no linter catches literal shell-outs) [MUST]
GO-IO-09 — Pass secrets to children via stdin or env, never argv (grep; G204 is not this check) [MUST]
GO-IO-10 — Classify timeout/cancel via ctx.Err()/context.Cause after Wait, never errors.Is(waitErr, DeadlineExceeded) (grep) [MUST]
GO-IO-11 — Write crash-surviving state only via CreateTemp-in-target-dir, write, Sync, checked Close, Rename, Unix dir fsync; never os.WriteFile on the final path [MUST]
GO-IO-12 — Remove the temp file only when the rename did not happen; no unconditional defer os.Remove in a renaming function (grep) [MUST]
GO-IO-13 — Spawn from exactly one internal SDK function carrying the only G204 suppression (grep count = 1) [SHOULD]

GO-IO-14 — Tear down the whole tree: Setpgid, build-tagged SIGTERM-to-group Cancel with pid-reuse guard, WaitDelay grace, post-Wait group SIGKILL sweep; Windows keeps default Kill [MUST for SDK and tool-wrapping CLIs]
GO-IO-15 — Capture via Cmd.Stdout/Stderr writers; drain every taken pipe concurrently; bound stderr, reject (never truncate) oversized stdout payloads [SHOULD]
GO-IO-16 — Reject Windows-reserved device names in externally-derived file names regardless of GOOS (table test on the Linux leg) [MUST]
GO-IO-17 — On Windows, retry the atomic rename a bounded number of times on sharing/access-denied only [SHOULD]
GO-IO-18 — Stage content-addressed blobs off the final path, verify size then digest before rename, treat existing same-digest target as success [SHOULD]
GO-IO-19 — Take cross-process locks via a GOOS split (flock / x/sys/windows LockFileEx) or gofrs/flock in CLIs; the SDK takes none [SHOULD]
GO-IO-20 — Build the SDK child's environment from an explicit allowlist [SHOULD]
conflicts_resolved: os.Root vs filepath.IsLocal as the confinement MUST: os.Root everywhere (fleet floor >=1.26); IsLocal only an early reject. Measured: G305 fires even on an IsLocal-guarded Join

Archive GODEBUG pin: files dive said //go:debug in main or env. go vet rejects //go:debug outside package main, so binaries pin in a go.mod godebug block (verified via go list DefaultGODEBUG) and libraries and the SDK reject names themselves
Permission thresholds: measured gosec defaults are 0750/0600, which flag conventional 0755/0644 (335+100 corpus literals). The fleet config pins G301 0755, G302/G306 0644

G204 as the secrets-in-argv check (subprocess dive rule 10): measured to fire on any non-constant argv, including the stdin twin. Replaced by a grep; G204 is suppressed once at the SDK's single spawn point
Subprocess dive claimed zero corpus Setpgid/job-object precedent: measured 11 Setpgid sites in 8 repos, all OS-constrained, plus containerd's Windows job-object twin

Kill ladder: WaitDelay already is the SIGTERM-to-Kill grace (exec.go:289-314, ladder test). Its escalation is leader-only, so a post-Wait group SIGKILL sweep is added (measured: a grandchild survives without it)
Cancel=Signal(SIGTERM) returns EWINDOWS on Windows (exec_windows.go:65-77), so Cancel is build-tagged and Windows keeps the default Kill
renameio (files dive SHOULD) is not adopted: SDK is stdlib-only (Q2), 0 corpus imports, and it exports nothing on Windows. One internal helper instead
gofrs/flock vs hand-rolled for the SDK: LockFileEx is not in syscall, so the stdlib-only SDK takes no locks (ocx owns them); CLIs use the GOOS split or gofrs
noctx ownership duplicated in context-contract rule 7 and subprocess rule 1: GO-IO owns the exec half, GO-NET the http half, GO-CONC cites both
execwait=2 placement: GO-TEST-12's CI leak check plus a go-diagnose step, never a runtime GO-IO rule (it panics the program)
Audit 9/92 extraction-guard rate: the re-read found 4/5 'unguarded' sites guarded by delegation or allowlist, so no exemplar is cited as a proven zip-slip

Does a directory Sync error? Does a job object assigned right after Start reap a grandchild spawned immediately? Does the GO-IO-16 validator pass?
io/process-group-sweep — is the post-Wait Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL) safe against pgid reuse once the group is empty, and is Linux Pdeathsig the right complement when the parent itself dies?
network/registry-client (wave 3) — absorb GO-IO-18 with a planted two-writer fixture: concurrent ingest of one digest, verify-before-rename, and rename-over-existing on Windows

surprises: staticcheck SA1005 does NOT ban /bin/sh -c shell-outs — it only flags a whole shell command jammed into argv[0] itself, and explicitly exempts any value containing '/', so '/bin/sh' as argv[0] is specifically excluded by the analyzer's own source; confirmed by running it on a planted violation that produced zero findings, overturning this dive's own initial reading of the brief

gosec G204 fires identically on exec.Command and exec.CommandContext — it gives no credit for using the context-aware constructor, and fires only on non-constant arguments, so a literal /bin/sh -c shell-out is completely invisible to it

WaitDelay bounds Wait even with plain exec.Command and NO context at all — the stdlib source shows awaitGoroutines starts its own timer whenever no context-derived timer exists, so a one-shot wrapper with no cancellation need still benefits from setting WaitDelay

A context-canceled child that dies BY SIGNAL reports through Wait as *exec.ExitError, never as context.DeadlineExceeded — the doc's context-error branch only fires when the child manages to exit with a SUCCESS status after Cancel runs, which a SIGTERM-killed child essentially never does

The GODEBUG=execwait=2 leak detector is entirely undocumented (absent from go.dev/doc/godebug, marked with a '#' prefix marking Go-internal tooling) and its failure mode is a hard panic with a captured creation stack trace, not a log line

No exemplar in the 35-repo corpus demonstrates the full recommended MUST shape (CommandContext + WaitDelay + Cancel + Setpgid) end-to-end — WaitDelay/Cancel adoption is 8/4 hits corpus-wide and zero exemplars combine them with process-group cancellation

archive/tar.Reader.Next() and archive/zip.NewReader/OpenReader are insecure by default in Go 1.27.1 -- ErrInsecurePath requires an explicit GODEBUG=...insecurepath=0 opt-in, and even then zip.NewReader still returns the malicious entries in .File alongside the error.

4 of 5 re-read 'unguarded' archive-extraction sites from the audit's 9/92 sample turned out to actually be guarded (containerd's fs.RootPath, cli/cli's safepaths+ghzip, syncthing/tailscale's allowlist-basename-plus-fixed-destination pattern) -- the audit's inline four-idiom regex undercounts real guard coverage.

filepath.IsLocal's Windows-reserved-name check is compiled only into the Windows build of internal/filepathlite -- on GOOS=linux, IsLocal('CON')/IsLocal('NUL') return true, a silent platform-dependent false negative.
gosec's own README.md and RULES.md contradict each other on what G307 means (old: deferred Close error handling; current: file-creation permissions) -- citing the README alone gets it wrong.
renameio exports nothing at all on Windows because atomic replace has no equivalent guarantee there (golang/go#22397); the fleet needs its own bounded remove-then-rename retry, not a port.

A successful atomic rename still leaves an orphaned .tmp file behind after a crash (confirmed on the sandbox) -- the atomic-write MUST is incomplete without a startup sweep for stale temp files, tying atomicity to on-disk format/versioning concerns.
